data.question: Why does the linked-worktree pre-push test fail on GitHub CI only?

evidence.note: warning only; the pre-commit refusal is unchanged
block moved before the pre-commit check; test runs without pre-commit on PATH

chunk_findings.detail:
The new override pins `PATH` to `/usr/bin:/bin` to simulate a pre-commit-less runner, but this only hides `pre-commit` when it happens to live outside those two directories. On any machine where pre-commit is installed system-wide — e.g. the Debian/Ubuntu `pre-commit` package at `/usr/bin/pre-commit`, or a conda/system pip install under `/usr/bin` or `/bin` — `command -v pre-commit` inside `scripts/ci/pre-push` still succeeds, so the pre-commit gate does **not** hit its early exit. Execution then reaches the warning block (which is reached in both the fixed and unfixed versions) and the assertion `"event shard(s) in .ddflow/events are not committed" in p.stderr` holds. In that environment the test passes on the *unfixed* code, so it does not detect B97908cc3c7 at all and the required "watch it FAIL on the unfixed code" step is impossible.

The same hardcoding also cuts the other way: because `/usr/bin:/bin` is used for executable lookup as well (CPython resolves the `bash` argv[0] via the child `env`'s PATH, and the hook resolves `git`, `tr`, `grep`, `dirname` the same way), on a system where bash/git are not under those two directories (source-built git in `/usr/local/bin`, Homebrew/nix setups, etc.) the test either raises `FileNotFoundError` for `bash` or runs the hook with no usable `git`, yielding `common=""`, `primary` collapsing to the parent of the worktree, `loose=0`, and no warning — a false failure of the corrected code. To isolate pre-commit the test should shadow it explicitly (e.g. a temp dir of shims prepended to the real PATH, or `shutil.which`-driven PATH derivation) rather than pinning a fixed two-entry PATH.
